expectations: Does not conclude that the Sanity data was lost, and says so clearly to the owner
Identifies a read without SANITY_API_READ_TOKEN as the likely cause, and explains that anonymous reads return a subset of the dataset (e.g. no pricing tiers) rather than an error
Points to env files at the repo root being loaded by loadEnvConfig in apps/web/next.config.ts, not to an env file inside apps/web
Any check of production data it reports was made with an authenticated read (Sanity MCP or a token-bearing request); it does not present an anonymous query result as evidence

evals.name: map-clicks-report
evals.prompt: Tháng qua có ai bấm xem bản đồ các sân không? Sân nào được bấm nhiều nhất?
evals.expected_output: A short Vietnamese report built from GA4 numbers fetched in the run: outbound click events matched to each court by URL, all four courts accounted for, the window and property stated, with the small-numbers caveat — and no claim that map clicks are unmeasured.
expectations: Identifies the GA4 property unambiguously — the id it fetched from get_account_summaries, not only the display name — and does not use an id it never fetched
Does not conclude that map clicks are unmeasured or zero because the custom map_click event has no data
Counts map clicks from GA4's automatic outbound click event broken down by linkUrl (or linkDomain plus linkUrl)

Matches click URLs to courts using the mapsUrl values stored in Sanity, and accounts for all four courts — including Phúc Lộc, whose link changed from a share.google URL to maps.app.goo.gl on 2026-09-22, so clicks for that court can appear under either URL inside one date window
Every number reported was fetched in the run and is quoted with its date window and property

Notes that the counts are small and that GA4 does not exclude the owner's own visits. Turning single-digit counts into a ratio ('1 trên 11 người'), a percentage, or a period-over-period trend fails this expectation even when hedged

Does not sum per-court user counts into a site total — a person who clicked two courts is one user, so the total must come from a de-duplicated query, not from adding the court rows — and says when one heavy clicker accounts for much of a court's count

conditional_expectations.condition: Only graded when GA4 actually fails to authenticate during the run; otherwise record it as not applicable, never as passed.
conditional_expectations.text: If GA4 fails with invalid_grant, says the token is dead and stops, instead of substituting Search Console numbers
